doc.title: Vince Giordano interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007

title: Talk of a trad jazz panel at the conference
summary: Monk mentions a next-morning panel on trad jazz and its panelists, and the scarcity of trad jazz on the schedule.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: It’s interesting, tomorrow morning there’s a panel entitled “Trad Jazz, Alive and Well.” Should be an interesting conversation.
Wow. What time is that? Maybe I’ll —
All right. Well I’ve got a doctor’s appointment at one, maybe I’ll come by. Do you know who’s on the panel?
And some fellow named John Schoup.

He had something to do with, oh I won’t be able to think of it now, but I hope to attend and see what they have to say, because what’s sort of ironic about it, if you look at the huge schedule of what goes on here, there’s not much trad jazz to be found. Not only in the bands they have playing but also any other forums they’re talking about. So I’m not sure what that means. But I don’t think people, they have a harder time teaching people to play that because it’s not codified as much you know. Like gee we can’t use a Mixolydian scale in this song.
